reasons: The finding is correctly characterized: p0080 is the sole assignment provision, it lacks an M&A/successor carve-out for Client, uses an unqualified consent standard, and contains no competitor bar — a genuine deviation from the preferred position but short of walk-away since the restriction is mutual and there is no vendor change-of-control termination/re-pricing right.

The redline reaches the preferred position with targeted insertions: (i) affiliate/successor carve-out for Client covering merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of substantially all assets, (ii) 'not unreasonably withheld or delayed' consent standard, (iii) bar on TrueLink assigning to a Client competitor, and (iv) express confirmation that a Client change of control is neither an assignment nor a TrueLink termination/suspension/re-pricing trigger.

Narrowing the pre-existing affiliate carve-out to Client only is directionally correct for our side and matches the preferred position that Vendor may not assign without our consent; the resulting clause remains grammatical and operative.

The failed 'minimal edit' check (0.672 changed-character ratio) is explained by the rule requiring four substantive additions to a single short sentence; no unnecessary language was altered, so the advisory flag does not warrant rejection.

The comment accurately describes each change, cites the playbook position on corporate reorganizations, and offers the mutual successor-with-notice fallback in the required concise, first-person-plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix.
